title: THE PRESSURE OF A BETTER OFFER

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Balak sent other officials, more numerous and more distinguished than the first. They came to Balaam and said: "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: Do not let anything keep you from coming to me, because I will reward you handsomely and do whatever you say. Come and put a curse on these people for me." - Num 22:15-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balak will not take no for an answer. He sends a second delegation, this time larger and more distinguished, carrying a bigger promise. The message is clear: name your price, and it is yours. Balak is turning up the pressure, and the temptation grows heavier.

This is how temptation often works. The first refusal is not the end of the matter. When we resist once, the offer frequently comes back sweeter and stronger, testing whether our conviction was firm or merely convenient. What we could easily decline yesterday becomes harder to refuse today.

Balaam had already heard God's clear word. There was nothing left to reconsider. Yet the increased reward dangled before him, and a heart not fully surrendered begins to wonder if there might be a way to have both God and the gold. Greed whispers that surely the rules can bend for a price like this.

Here is where we must be watchful. When God has spoken clearly, a bigger temptation does not change His word; it only tests our hearts. The love of money has led many astray (1 Tim 6:10). But in Christ we have a treasure that no earthly reward can match. Hold fast to His clear word, whatever the offer.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you respond when temptation returns stronger after you have resisted?
2. Where might greed be tempting you to reconsider what God has clearly said?
3. What treasure in Christ helps you say no to lesser rewards?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when temptation returns with a sweeter offer, keep me anchored to Your clear word. Guard my heart from greed and satisfy me with the treasure I have in Christ. Amen.
